title: API Token Governance: Scoped Keys, Rotation SOPs, and Admin Visibility
creator: Priya Shah
description: Define and implement a production-ready API token governance model aligned with RBAC v2 and audit logging improvements. Scope: per-scope keys (service, user, embedding-only, admin), naming conventions, automated rotation/expiry, token metadata surfaced in Console, admin controls for forced revocation, and audit events for creation/rotation/revocation. Deliverables include API changes, Console UI updates, runtime enforcement hooks, and SSO/SAML integration notes for session-vs-token lifecycle. Work replaces ad-hoc token naming and manual rotation with a standardized, auditable workflow and operator tooling.
acceptance_criteria: New API supports creation of scoped keys with explicit scope list and optional expiry TTL
Admin console surfaces active tokens with metadata: creator, created_at, scope, last_used_at, expiry, and fingerprint
Rotation endpoint that issues a new key, automatically retires old key, and writes full audit trail
Forced revocation invalidates token in runtime caches within SLA (<= 5s) and writes audit events
Audit log entries exist for create/rotate/revoke with actor, IP, SAML session id (if available), and request id
Migration path for existing long-lived keys (notify owners, set mandatory expiry, allow grace period)
Security review sign-off and small-scale load test to validate rotation path under active traffic
tasks: Design API contract: POST /v1/tokens (scopes[], name, expiry_seconds) and POST /v1/tokens/:id/rotate
Backend: token store schema changes (add scopes, name, created_by, last_used_at, fingerprint)
Runtime: extend auth middleware to enforce scope checks and fast revocation via in-memory tombstones
Console: Admin token list UI + token creation modal with recommended naming patterns
Audit: emit structured audit events to the logging pipeline for token lifecycle operations
SSO/SAML: map SAML attributes to token creator metadata and surface session_id in audit when present
Migration: script to tag existing keys for mandatory expiry and initial owner notification email
Docs: security playbook and rotation SOP published in Confluence + customer-facing KB article
decisions: Use per-key scope model (explicit allow-list) instead of role-synthesis on token creation to keep evaluation cheap at runtime
Implement rotation as atomic create+revoke to avoid in-place secret mutation and preserve audit history
Fingerprint tokens using SHA256 truncated hex and store only fingerprint in DB to avoid persistent plaintext secrets
Enforce default max TTL of 90 days for new tokens unless "admin-exempt" flag is used (admin-exempt requires security approval)
Fast revocation will be implemented with a distributed tombstone cache propagated via existing config bus for sub-5s invalidation
tradeoffs: Per-key scope evaluation simplifies policy reasoning but increases token count and management surface for customers
Storing only fingerprints increases security but complicates some customer support flows (we must rely on issued token fingerprints for lookup)
Forced short TTLs reduce blast radius but will increase operational load for customers that use long-lived CI tokens; mitigated by recommending dedicated service tokens
Immediate revocation via distributed cache adds complexity to runtime but required for strong admin controls and compliance
risks: Possible increased load on token creation/rotation endpoints during mass rotation (mitigate with rate limits and rollout schedule)
Customer confusion during migration if naming/expiry enforced without clear communication
SSO/SAML attribute mappings may be inconsistent across enterprise IdPs leading to incomplete audit records
migration_plan: Phase 1: Feature flag deploy (read+write) of token metadata and rotation endpoints; Phase 2: Console UI behind opt-in; Phase 3: Notify customers and enable mandatory expiry for legacy tokens with 30-day grace; Phase 4: Enforce new defaults and begin security-mandated rotation for admin-exempt tokens after approvals.
notes: Coordinate with Platform Reliability (PR #3120) for cache propagation changes and with Support to prepare lookup utilities. Schedule joint tabletop with PM and Legal for compliance language in customer KB.
